meta.disclosure: Illustrative sample trends written for the ShowStop demo. They describe common short-video formats in general terms. They are not real posts, creators or measurements, and every signal is a qualitative illustration.
meta.label: Sample trend
meta.observationWindow: Illustrative. No observation period was measured.

stages.emerging: Few creators use it yet. Early, but the format is still unproven.
stages.rising: Spreading across niches. A good time to adapt it.
stages.peaking: Widely used. Needs a strong twist to stand out.
stages.fading: Viewers have seen it often. Use only with a clear reason.

media.video: Short vertical video. In the demo, video items are described, not playable.

trends.title: One thing, three ways
trends.summary: A creator takes one everyday item and shows three different uses in under 30 seconds.
trends.whyItWorks: The promise is clear in the first second, each use is a small payoff, and viewers save it to try later.
examples: One can of chickpeas turned into three meals
keep: The number three in the hook
One item on screen at the start
A quick cut between each use

signals.label: Viewer response
signals.value: Comments ask for a fourth way

trends.limits: Saves and comments are described, not counted. Works best when each use is genuinely different.

reasons: Budget ingredients stretched three ways match Maya's audience
Each use can be filmed in one short session
unknowns: Whether Maya's audience prefers full recipes or quick ideas

reasons: One thrifted item styled three ways suits small spaces
unknowns: Whether one item gives enough visual change on camera

trends.keywords: cheap budget dinner meal food recipe cook one ingredient three ways roommates student style decor mirror

trends.title: Day 1 vs Day 30
trends.summary: A split or jump cut compares the first attempt with the result after a month of practice or change.
trends.whyItWorks: Progress is satisfying to watch, and the contrast does the storytelling.
examples: A room on move-in day and a month later
A first and thirtieth attempt at the same dish
keep: The same camera angle for both shots

signals.label: Effort to make
signals.value: High, needs planning a month ahead

trends.limits: A peaking format needs a twist. Requires footage from the start, which a creator may not have.

reasons: Learning to cook on a budget is a natural progress story
unknowns: Whether a month of daily cooking fits Maya's schedule

reasons: Room makeovers are a natural before and after
Afternoon light keeps both shots consistent
unknowns: Whether a current project already has before footage

trends.keywords: progress month before after room makeover learn skill change

trends.title: Silent process
trends.summary: A calm, wordless video of a task from start to finish, with natural sound and short captions.
trends.whyItWorks: It is relaxing, watchable without sound on, and keeps the focus on the hands and the result.
examples: Cooking dinner with only kitchen sounds
Repotting a plant with captions for each step
keep: No voice or music over the natural sound
trends.limits: Noisy spaces make it harder. Captions must carry the key information.

reasons: Maya prefers not to talk on camera
Cooking sounds are part of the appeal
unknowns: How loud the shared kitchen is during filming windows

reasons: Makeover steps can be shown without talking
unknowns: Whether makeover viewers want the reasoning behind choices

trends.keywords: calm quiet no talking silent relaxing asmr process captions shy

trends.title: Things I stopped buying
trends.summary: A creator lists things they no longer buy and what they do instead.
trends.whyItWorks: It feels honest and useful, and viewers compare it with their own habits in the comments.
examples: Grocery items swapped for cheaper staples
Decor items replaced with thrifted ones

signals.label: Spread
signals.value: Common in money and home niches

trends.limits: Peaking, so a specific angle matters. Avoid naming brands negatively.

reasons: Budget swaps are exactly Maya's audience's problem
Easy to film with items already in the kitchen
unknowns: Whether Maya wants to say what not to buy rather than what to cook
Whether renters relate to the items chosen

trends.keywords: save money budget cheap swap stopped buying groceries thrift honest list

trends.title: POV: you just moved in
trends.summary: On-screen text puts the viewer in a situation, here an empty new place, and the video shows what happens next.
trends.whyItWorks: Viewers place themselves in the story, and the text hook works without sound.
examples: POV: you just moved into a studio with no furniture
keep: The POV caption in the first frame
Filming from the viewer's eye level
trends.limits: Fading. Use it only if the situation itself is fresh or very specific.

reasons: Moving in is not Maya's topic
unknowns: A 'first meal in a new kitchen' version might work, but it would be a different story

reasons: Empty rental rooms are Jordan's starting point
unknowns: Whether the fading stage reduces interest

trends.keywords: moved new apartment studio rental empty room pov renter

trends.title: Rate it honestly
trends.summary: A creator tries something and gives an honest score out of ten, often as a numbered series.
trends.whyItWorks: A score is an easy payoff to wait for, and a series brings viewers back.
examples: Rating cheap dorm snacks out of ten
keep: The score revealed at the end

signals.label: Viewer response
signals.value: Comments suggest what to rate next

trends.limits: Emerging, so the payoff is uncertain. Ratings of named products need care.

reasons: Rating budget recipes suits a series
unknowns: Whether Maya wants to appear on camera for reactions

reasons: Rating does not show Jordan's makeover skills
unknowns: A 'rating my thrift finds' version might work

trends.keywords: rate review score honest try test snacks series reaction
